paths.description: Homepage and current-results dashboard, representing the dense primary landing template and result lookup task.
Southern lottery results listing, representing regional result/listing templates.
Southern live-results page, representing the time-sensitive live result journey.
Account registration form, representing the separately styled responsive forum/account flow.
Contact/feedback form, representing the primary form and recovery/validation surface.
Unknown URL, representing HTTP/network failure recovery.

findings.summary: The main site ignores the user’s dark-theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-condition screenshot is visually the same white/red surface as the default; computed color-scheme is normal and no dark-theme CSS signal was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Text and controls do not consistently survive contrast requirements.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored color-contrast 0, and the contrast screenshot plus 11px base text show low-contrast dense labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use tested semantic color tokens meeting WCAG contrast, retain control boundaries in forced colors, and verify at high contrast.

findings.summary: Navigation changes are abrupt and provide no transition continuity.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition usage across a navigation-heavy MPA.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-origin navigation with @view-transition { navigation: auto } and stable view-transition-name values.

findings.summary: The dense navigation and repeated link groups do not establish a clear location or attention path.
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains several competing nav rows, side lists and data tables; no nav/main landmarks were present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic navigation and main landmarks, clear current-page state, and a single dominant route into each core task.

findings.summary: Large animated promotions compete with and displace the result content.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show multiple prominent animated GIF ads around the primary lottery results; ad imagery accounts for most transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer non-essential promotions, reserve limited non-animated ad slots, and keep the current result content dominant.

findings.summary: The main template is visually crowded and difficult to scan.
findings.evidence: The 360px capture renders an entire 1050px desktop canvas at 0.343 scale, with tiny repeated tables, sidebars and banners.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild the content hierarchy around the current draw/result, collapse secondary lists, and use readable spacing and typography.

findings.summary: Most primary templates are desktop layouts scaled down on phones.
findings.evidence: Home, results, live and contact lack viewport meta; at a requested 360px viewport Chrome lays out a 1050px canvas at 0.343 scale. Only the separate registration template is responsive.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a correct viewport meta tag and replace fixed-width columns/tables with intrinsic responsive layouts and narrow-screen reflow.

findings.summary: Reusable result and navigation components do not adapt to their available space.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container/container-type support and 250 physical-direction declarations; the same fixed multi-column components are scaled on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable components containment and adapt table/card/nav layouts with container queries and intrinsic sizing.

findings.summary: Touch targets are too small and focus is often invisible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse target-size scored 0; the probe found many 13–23px-high controls and registration text fields computed outline:none while focused.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44px practical touch targets, visible :focus-visible styles, and non-hover affordances.

findings.summary: Failure and form states do not provide robust recovery.
findings.evidence: An unknown URL returns HTTP 200 and only a POST button to home; the contact form marks no field required and exposes no aria-live/alert error region.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 with useful links/search, and add explicit loading/empty/error states with retry, preserved context and accessible form errors.

findings.summary: Mobile loading misses the LCP target.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 9.4s and performance 0.68; the trace corroborated LCP 2.80s under a lighter desktop condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Identify the LCP element, make it discoverable and high priority, and defer below-fold ads and non-critical assets.

findings.summary: Image-heavy delivery delays primary content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 63 requests and 2.71MB transferred, including 2.33MB of images; two GIF ads were about 0.5MB each. 43 below-fold images were not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Convert imagery to modern formats, lazy-load below-fold assets, preload only the true LCP asset, and eliminate unnecessary animated GIF variants.

findings.summary: The page loads avoidable duplicate and third-party code.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection shows jquery-3.2.1.js included twice; Google Tag Manager contributes about 180KB and multiple rotating ad variants load together.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate jQuery, audit old scripts for actual use, and load analytics/advertising only when justified and deferred.

findings.summary: Core controls, images and data tables lack accessible semantics.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility was 0.43 with failures for button/link names, labels, image alt, select names and table headers; the image audit found 60/60 images without alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful names/labels/alt text, mark decoration empty-alt, and associate lottery data cells with proper table headers.

findings.summary: Document structure and keyboard focus are weak.
findings.evidence: No semantic landmarks were found, multiple H1s are used, Lighthouse flagged heading order and missing main landmark, and focused fields often have outline:none.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce header/nav/main/footer landmarks, one coherent heading hierarchy, logical DOM order and visible focus styles.

findings.summary: The primary experience does not reflow into a usable mobile/zoom layout.
findings.evidence: Four representative main-site templates omit viewport meta and are rendered as tiny desktop canvases; target-size also failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Support 320 CSS px reflow without loss, preserve zoom, enlarge targets, and test at 200–400% zoom.

findings.summary: The document/assets contain structural and image hygiene problems.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a missing/invalid doctype on its audited response; 35 images lack dimensions, seven are oversized, and all 60 use legacy formats.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a standards-mode HTML5 document consistently and add intrinsic dimensions, responsive sources and modern formats.

findings.summary: Crawler configuration and mobile indexing signals are broken.
findings.evidence: robots.txt returns an HTML “URL does not exist” page and Lighthouse reports 30 robots errors; main templates have no viewport meta.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a valid text/plain robots.txt, point it to a real sitemap, and add viewport metadata to every public template.

findings.summary: Public pages lack coherent canonical/sitemap signals.
findings.evidence: No canonical or hreflang was found on the homepage, and both /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml return the same HTML error body with HTTP 200.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs per template, a valid XML sitemap, and correct status/content types; remove accidental soft-200 errors.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS but baseline security headers and cookie protections are missing.
findings.evidence: CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent; all three observed cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrictive CSP, HSTS and nosniff; set Secure and an appropriate Lax/Strict SameSite policy on first-party cookies.

findings.summary: Tracking runs by default without an evident minimisation choice.
findings.evidence: Four third-party origins load, including Google Tag Manager and DoubleClick; analytics cookies last 400 days and GTM transfers about 180KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise analytics fields/retention, gate optional tracking on informed consent where required, and batch/defer telemetry.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers inspection found no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy in addition to no CSP/HSTS; X-Frame-Options DENY is the only listed defense present.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, retain clickjacking protection, and consider CSP frame-ancestors and Trusted Types after removing unsafe patterns.

findings.summary: Forms do not expose humane, accessible validation.
findings.evidence: The contact form marks no user field required and has no aria-live or role=alert region; registration inputs suppress focus outlines and several date/location controls lack labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Use native constraints, validate after interaction, associate clear messages with fields, and announce an error summary accessibly.

findings.summary: Sign-up and contact fields do not use useful autofill semantics.
findings.evidence: Registration name/password fields use autocomplete=off or empty tokens; contact name, address, telephone and email fields also have empty autocomplete.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply correct username, new-password, name, address, tel and email autocomplete tokens and suitable input types.

findings.summary: Decorative and advertising assets consume disproportionate resources.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 60 legacy-format images, 43 eager below-fold images and no modern formats; images transfer 2.33MB of the 2.71MB page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use AVIF/WebP where suitable, responsive sources, lazy loading and static reduced-motion alternatives to animated GIFs.

findings.summary: Media and third-party loading are not proportionate to the core text/data task.
findings.evidence: Multiple large animated ad variants and 180KB GTM load on a lottery-results page; third-party tracking continues in the background.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight budget, load one appropriately sized ad only when visible, and defer/minimise third-party work.

taskList.title: Restore semantic accessibility and keyboard focus
Cut and defer animated image/ad weight to improve LCP
Reduce chrome and establish a clear content/navigation hierarchy
Add security headers and safe cookie policy
Repair robots, sitemap, canonical and soft-404 signals
Make forms humane, labelled and autofill-friendly
Standardise document and image asset hygiene
